title: Preemptible backfill and iso-routing PRD (wip)
summary: Sketch for a complementary dedicated-capacity feature that allows idle GPU slots to be offered as preemptible backfill for lower-priority tenants while preserving isolation and SLO guarantees for higher tiers. Introduces iso-routing lanes and a soft-preempt API to enable safe preemption, accounting, and rapid failover.
problem_statement: Dedicated pools often have transient idle capacity between peaks. Current options are: reserved-only (wasted cycles) or elastic burst into public pools (security and latency concerns). We need a way to monetize or utilize short-lived idle capacity without risking high-priority tenants' SLOs or tenant isolation. Also want explicit controls for customers to opt into giving/receiving backfill in predictable economic terms.
goals: 1) Capture value from short idle GPU time by offering preemptible backfill slots to lower-priority workloads. 2) Maintain strong isolation and fast recovery for primary tenant requests. 3) Provide clear APIs and billing signals so tenants can opt-in and set constraints. 4) Keep operational complexity manageable for on-call.
non_goals: 1) Not building a full market/exchange for spot trading across customers. 2) Not replacing Dedicated reserved capacity guarantees for customers who require hard isolation. 3) Not attempting aggressive model-level QoE optimizations (e.g., quantization switching) as part of this feature.
requirements: R1: Backfill tasks must be preemptible within a deterministic window (max preemption notification 250ms).
R2: High-priority tenant requests always have preemption precedence; preemption latency from decision to reclaim must be <100ms for new tokens.
R3: Customers must be able to opt their workloads into three modes: none, soft-backfill (best-effort, billed at discount), hard-backfill (aggressive preemption but higher discount).
R4: Isolation guarantees: memory/KV caches of primary tenants must never be reclaimed for backfill; backfill must run in sandboxed containers/nvlinks with bounded shared resources.
R5: API surface: autoscale policy must accept backfill_allowed: boolean and backfill_mode: {none, soft, hard}, plus priority_score and max_backfill_duration.
R6: Billing: preemptible usage reported separately with discount rate and backfill reclaim counts. Billing events must be produced for each preemption.
R7: Observability: metrics for backfill occupancy, preemption-rate, reclaim-latency, recovery-success-rate, and cost-savings estimate required.
R8: Rollout must include a canary phase limited to internal tenants and synthetic workloads and fail-open to not impact normal serving paths.
proposed_design: High level: introduce a BackfillDaemon in the dedicated pool manager that maintains an inventory of idle GPU slots and offers them to tenants that opt-in. Each slot is tagged with an iso-route label (hot-lane, warm-lane, backfill-lane) used by the request router. When primary traffic increases, the reclaim controller issues a soft-preempt signal to running backfill containers, triggering either graceful shutdown (soft) or immediate token drain (hard).
components: Inventory tracker: per-pool view of idle capacity with time-series of idle durations (helps pricing & decisions)
Backfill allocator: policy engine that matches queued backfill jobs to idle slots based on tenant opt-in mode, size, and predicted reclaim risk
Iso-routing tags: network/routing layer labels used by request router to prefer hot-lane for primary traffic; backfill lanes are routed to preemptible workloads
Preempt API: small runtime contract exposed to workloads (soft_preempt_signal with estimated grace_ms) and agent-side checkpoint hooks
Billing emitter: records preemptible runtime and preemption events for invoicing and internal chargebacks
Observability dashboard: per-pool + per-tenant views for occupancy, preemption latency, failover success
safety_and_isolation: Backfill tasks run under reduced privileges and quota-limited cgroups. KV caches are off-limits for eviction; backfill must never write to shared persistent volumes owned by primary tenants. Network and inter-instance NVLink resources are fenced. Reclaim path includes: (1) soft_preempt signal, (2) short grace period (configurable), (3) forced kill and requeue.
billing_and_pricing: Two-tiered discount approach: soft-backfill = 45% discount off list dedicated price, hard-backfill = 65% discount. Billing line-items show gross-hours, reclaimed-hours, and preemption-requests. For internal reporting compute realized utilization uplift and estimated offset to reserved cost.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): run synthetic ML inference workloads on a single dev pool to validate reclaim latency and metrics. Phase 1 (trusted customers): invite 3 customers to opt-in with explicit contracts, observe for 4 weeks. Phase 2 (general availability): enable self-serve opt-in in the Console with default soft-backfill disabled for new pools. Phase gates: preemption <100ms median, recovery-success-rate >99% on primary requests.
operational_runbooks: Runbook 1: High preemption rate alert -> Inspect pool idle time series, backfill_accept_rate, and recent traffic surge. If preemption spikes because of misconfigured opt-in, roll back opt-ins for affected tenants.
Runbook 2: Reclaim latency regression -> Revert BackfillDaemon change, scale controller to emergency mode, and open P0 incidence to infra team.
Runbook 3: Billing mismatch -> Reconcile preemption events with invoice emitter and re-run accumulator job. Notify finance within 24h.
open_questions: Q1: What contractual language is required for offering preemptible discounts to enterprise customers? (legal/finance)
Q2: How to instrument graceful model checkpointing generically for arbitrary inference containers? (platform/applied-ml)
Q3: Should backfill be allowed in cross-tenant private deployments when customers require strict VPC isolation?
Q4: Pricing: fixed discount vs dynamic micro-market? Start with fixed for simplicity.
Q5: Can we integrate with Optimize to recommend which customers should opt into backfill based on workload profiles?
approx_effort_estimate: 3 sprints infra (BackfillDaemon + reclaim controller) + 2 sprints platform (APIs + billing) + 1 sprint product/console + QA & canary ~4 weeks
success_criteria: 1) Increase average pool utilization by >= 12% in canary pools without measurable impact to primary p99 latency. 2) Preemption median latency <100ms and recovery-success-rate >= 99.5%. 3) First cohort customers receive accurate billing and report expected cost savings.
appendix: Example flow: 1) Pool has 4 idle slots for 3 minutes. 2) BackfillAllocator assigns two low-priority jobs in soft mode. 3) Primary tenant traffic spikes -> router marks two slots needed, BackfillDaemon sends soft_preempt with grace_ms=150. 4) Jobs checkpoint (if implemented) and exit within grace period; reclaim completes and primary requests land on reclaimed GPUs within 90ms. 5) Billing shows 0.05 reclaimed_hours and 2 preemption events.
notes_to_self: Need to sync with legal and list of pilot customers. Get infra benchmark on preempt path for GPU types (A100, H100). Coordinate with SRE on alert thresholds.
